Would a keyboard user meet these elements in an order that makes sense for reading and using this part of the page? question.rubric: The question is whether the order keeps the page's meaning and lets a keyboard user operate it, not whether it matches the order drawn on the screen: an order that differs from the drawn one is not does_not_preserve by itself. does_not_preserve: related fields split apart (the address fields interleaved with other fields); numbered steps, or any items whose order is the point (a timeline, a form's fields), reached out of sequence; a Shift+Tab order that jumps around so going back makes no sense; focus jumping back and forth between unrelated areas; a menu's or dialog's content reached far from its trigger; a positive tabindex sending focus to an unrelated place first. preserves: columns read one after another; a grid of cards, or columns of footer links, read row by row with each card's or item's parts together (its image link, then its title link); tiles in a row or a slider reached from right to left or left to right when each tile is independent and its own parts stay together; one tile's own buttons reached in another order than drawn (a Share button before its Save button); a side list's sub-items reached right after their parent item; main content reached before side navigation that comes later in the document; header, navigation, main, footer; a skip link first; independent sidebars in either order. does_not_matter: independent items whose order cannot change meaning, such as a row of social media icons. unsure: whenever the evidence does not settle it (the image does not show the numbered elements the signals name clearly; the grouping that matters is not visible; you cannot tell whether the items are independent or a sequence; the content is in a language you cannot read). question.question: input.items are the fields and buttons of one form, in page order, with the label people see for each (label), text near it (near), its group's label (group) and, for fields, a picture (image); a field may be labelled only by the picture on a button beside it (icon_buttons_beside_it). Taken with what is around them, does each label make clear what to enter (including any format the field needs, such as a date) or what the button does? Answer all_descriptive, some_not_descriptive (put the numbers of the ones that are not in elements) or unsure.
question.rubric: descriptive: names what to enter or do, even in one word ("First name", "Search" next to a search box, "Name" under a visible "Billing address" heading or group label). not descriptive: unrelated or empty of meaning ("Menu", "Info", "The sky is blue", "Field 1"), the same label on several fields with nothing visible to tell them apart, a date or number field whose required format appears only in an error message. A placeholder is not a label. A button's words beside a field say what to enter only when they name it ("Search" beside a search box); words that say only what the button does ("Submit", "Send", "OK") do not. A field whose only label is the picture on a button beside it (icon_buttons_beside_it; look at image): descriptive when the picture is a symbol commonly understood for what to enter (a magnifier on a search box, an envelope on an email field, a calendar on a date field); not descriptive when it is unrelated to the field or names something else (a flower or a company logo on a search box, a telephone on an email field). unsure: whenever the picture or text does not settle it.
